titular: US inflation surprises on the upside again in October
resum: US prices rose 0.4% in October from September, a tenth of a point more than expected. Core inflation, which strips out energy and food, rose 0.3%, also above the 0.2% forecast.
per_que_importa: If prices keep rising faster than they should, the Federal Reserve will raise rates and borrowing will get more expensive in the US and, by knock-on effect, in markets around the world. For you, it means cheap money won't be back any time soon.

titular: Markets now take a December Fed rate hike for granted
resum: After the inflation data, futures markets put the chance of a December rate hike at 100%. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said even a half-point hike should be considered if inflation doesn't ease.
per_que_importa: The Fed's rates set the price of money in the world's largest economy: when they rise, mortgages, credit cards and business loans get dearer, which ends up slowing investment and hiring.
xifra_text: chance markets give to a Fed hike in December

titular: Wall Street falls and the US 10-year bond yield hits 5%
resum: The Nasdaq lost 0.74% and the S&P 500 0.38% on Tuesday, dragged down by tech stocks. Nvidia fell 5.5% as its board investigates CEO Jensen Huang, and the 10-year bond yield moved close to 5%.
per_que_importa: When government debt pays almost 5% risk-free, shares become less attractive and companies that need funding pay more for it. It's a reminder that high rates weigh on the whole stock market.

titular: ECB's Lane sees a December rate hike as prudent
resum: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said that if December's data look like today's, raising rates would be "very prudent". He expects euro-area inflation to end the year slightly above 4%.
per_que_importa: An ECB hike would push the Euribor even higher and, with it, payments on variable-rate mortgages. On the other hand, savings accounts and Spanish Treasury bills (Letras del Tesoro) could pay a little more.
xifra_text: euro-area inflation Lane expects at year-end

titular: The Ibex touches 20,000 points and breaks through this morning
resum: Spain's Ibex 35 rose 0.98% on Tuesday to 19,936.4 points after touching 20,000 for the first time during the session, driven by banks (CaixaBank, +3.3%). On Wednesday it opened above the round number, at around 20,064 points.
per_que_importa: The Spanish stock market is up more than 15% this year, mainly thanks to banks, which benefit from high rates. Many pension plans and funds hold part of people's savings there.

titular: 24-hour general strike in Spain over housing costs and wages
resum: The CCOO and UGT unions have called Spain's first general strike in 14 years today, protesting about housing costs and wages. It affects flights (Barcelona El Prat, Girona and Reus), trains and the Barcelona metro, which must guarantee 25% of service at peak times.
per_que_importa: It shows how far housing has become the biggest economic problem for many families. A strike day also has a cost in lost output for businesses and in travel disruption for people.

titular: Siemens Energy soars and lifts European stocks close to a record
resum: Europe's Stoxx 600 index was up 0.7% in early trading, just shy of its all-time high from August. Siemens Energy gained 6.5% on forecasts of higher margins in 2027 and a dividend set to more than triple, while Vestas fell 6% on lower-than-expected profits.
per_que_importa: Siemens Energy makes turbines and power-grid equipment that are in high demand from data centres and the energy transition: an example of how the AI boom is also reaching traditional industry.
xifra_text: Siemens Energy's rise in early trading

titular: SoftBank loses $7bn on its AI bets
resum: Japan's SoftBank posted a loss of about ¥1.1 trillion (around $7bn) for July to September, compared with a ¥2.5 trillion profit a year earlier. Meanwhile, the rest of Asia is rising on chip demand: Taiwan +3.6%, South Korea +2.4% and Tokyo +1.3%.
per_que_importa: SoftBank is one of OpenAI's biggest investors: its losses show that AI valuations can fall just as they rise, and that money put into them carries significant risk.

titular: Oil drops to its lowest since August and gold also falls
resum: Brent closed on Tuesday at $91.49 a barrel (−1.2%), its lowest since 31 August, after Trump suggested the war with Iran could end soon. Gold fell more than 2% to around $4,030 an ounce; today crude is edging back up after attacks on ships in Hormuz.
per_que_importa: Cheaper oil eventually reaches the petrol pump and makes transporting goods cheaper, which helps curb inflation. On the Spanish stock market, however, it hits oil companies such as Repsol (−2.3%).

titular: Today: the US bond market closes, and Spain's final CPI arrives on Friday
resum: For Veterans Day, US stocks are open but the bond market and most banks are closed. Industrial prices and weekly jobless claims come out in the US over the next few days, and on Friday the 13th Spain's statistics office (INE) will confirm October's inflation (4.9% in the flash estimate).
per_que_importa: The final CPI is used to update rental contracts and other prices linked to inflation, and will show whether October's price rise is confirmed.
xifra_text: Spain's flash October inflation, to be confirmed on Friday
